g.text: A waveform viewer that lives in your terminal
Scope tree, grouped signals, buses, analog rows and cursor readouts — pure Python, no dependencies, no display server. Works the
same over SSH, in tmux, on a bare console.
Give the waves the whole width
s hides or shows the hierarchy pane; Tab moves focus between the pane and the waves.
+ and - zoom around the cursor, ←→ or h/l pan, Z fits the whole trace, W fits between cursors A and B. Everything is
vim-friendly: j/k, gg, G, Shift+↑↓ jump between modules.

text.tspan: ◆ Find Signal — type to filter · ↑↓ Navigate · Tab Mark · Enter Add & Jump · Esc Cancel
• already displayed · ▪ marked │ space AND-terms · Ctrl-U clear · Ctrl-W del word

g.text: Fuzzy-find any signal in the file
/ filters every signal as you type, fzf-style. ↑↓ choose, Tab marks several, Enter adds them to the view and jumps there.
Fuzzy-find any signal in the file
state is now on screen and focused. Signals already displayed are marked •; the finder never loses your place.
x splits the focused bus into per-bit lanes (x again folds them). F does the same for float fields: sign, exponent, mantissa,
R cycles the focused signal's radix — hex, dec, unsigned, bin, f16/f32/f64 — while r changes all of them. Enum decode maps
Search with an expression over signals
The ; prompt is the command line. ;when jumps the cursor to the first time a boolean expression holds: &&, ||, !, comparisons,
hex/bin literals, any signal in the file.
Search with an expression over signals
Cursor A lands at the first handshake. The status line echoes where and why; n repeats a search, ;find moves focus by name.
1 and 2 place cursors A and B; ] and [ snap the active cursor to the next or previous edge of the focused signal. The status bar
;glitches scans the trace for runt pulses, zero-width glitches and transitions into x, counts them and jumps to the next one.
;stats reads the focused signal over the window or between cursors: transitions, period and frequency, duty cycle — min/max for
buses. e measures edge to edge.
m drops a labelled marker at the cursor; < and > jump between markers, ;marker 220ns places one by time. A adds a note on a
signal or an interval; both persist in sidecars.
F12 manages markers: filter by label or time, Enter jumps, u / Ctrl-R undo and redo.
;group bundles signals under a collapsible header (nest with parent/child), Tab folds the focused header. V selects a range
visually; J/K reorder; u undoes any layout change.

text.tspan: ◆ Signal Browser — ↑↓ Navigate · → Expand · ← Collapse · Space Toggle · Enter Select Scope · B Close

g.text: B opens the full-screen browser of every module and signal in the file. → expands a scope, Space adds or removes a signal, Enter

text.tspan: ◆ Signal Browser — ↑↓ Navigate · → Expand · ← Collapse · Space Toggle · Enter Select Scope · B Close

g.text: Ticks show what is on screen; toggling a signal updates the waves behind the browser.
\ cycles the built-in themes; ;theme loads one by name or from a JSON file. True-colour #rrggbb themes quantize gracefully on
Light, dark, calm, minimal, phosphor, futuristic, mono — or your own.

text.tspan: Search for short pulses and unknown values
↑↓ Choose · Enter Run · Esc Back · Ctrl-U Clear

g.text: F4 or Ctrl-P opens a palette of all actions with their shortcuts; type to filter, Enter runs. ? is the quick reference, F1 the
;session writes a sidecar next to the trace — layout, groups, radixes, colours, zoom, theme — and reopening restores it. X
exports SVG; E opens the export menu (CSV, PDF, screenshot, pixel-accurate PNG).
Started with --control, an MCP client (or any local agent) can group, search, zoom and mark this live session while you watch —
the ◆AGENT badge shows when it acts. --mcp also serves headless snapshots of any trace.
